item.title: BU Student Government confirms leadership roles, approves funding requests in first meeting of the semester
item.description: The Boston University Student Government met Monday to review its budget, confirm new executive and judicial appointments and pass two funding requests from student organizations.

item.title: The murder of Wael Tarabishi and the intersections of disability and racial imperialism | The Dissenting Opinion
item.description: On Jan. 23, Wael Tarabishi died in hospice care without his father by his side. The 30-year-old lived with Pompe disease, a condition requiring 24/7 care and medical support. item.title: Why are kids not being kids anymore?
item.description: Children want to look like tweens, tweens long to look like teenagers, teenagers want to look like grown women and grown women long to have clear, wrinkle-free skin like they did as children — a vicious cycle of trying to reach an unobtainable ideal.

item.title: BU COM dean corresponded extensively with Jeffrey Epstein in 2014 and 2015, files show
item.description: Mariette DiChristina, dean of Boston University’s College of Communication, corresponded extensively with Jeffrey Epstein in 2014 and 2015. The two set up a one-on-one meeting, had “phone dates” and DiChristina invited him to attend an editorial meeting for the Scientific American, where she worked as editor-in-chief. item.title: Can Aston Villa win the Premier League?
item.description: Aston Villa Football Club entered the 2025-26 Premier League season projected to finish just outside the top six. Fast forward four weeks, and they failed to score in their first four games — leaving them the lowest-scoring team across the top ten divisions of English football.

item.title: On the Hill: Team USA alpine skiing goes for gold at the Olympics
item.description: The 2026 Winter Olympic Games in Milano Cortina are set to take off in just a few days’ time. The opening ceremony is scheduled for Friday, Feb. 6, at 2 p.m. EST.

item.title: Susan Fournier to retire after eight years as Questrom Dean, 21 years at BU
item.description: Susan Fournier, dean of the Questrom School of Business since 2018, announced Jan. 23 she will step down from her role on June 30, ending her eight year run as dean.

item.description: Boston University students and community members picketed outside the Howard Thurman Center for Common Ground Wednesday evening, protesting a BU Students for Israel event hosting Adi Karni, an Israel Defense Forces soldier, who fought in both Gaza and Lebanon. item.title: BU track and field athletes claim BU failed to adequately support team amid Zac Segal controversy
item.description: Multiple members of the Boston University track and field team claimed administrators failed to adequately support them following nationwide backlash sparked by a controversial social media post from teammate and BU College Republicans president Zac Segal.
